topology: Two client LANs enter R1 independently. The prepared RIB prefers R1 → R2 → R4 for SRV1 and a diagnostic R4 loopback. A second R1 → R3 → R4 path supplies the adjacent policy next hop10.0.13.2. Static routes and independent return paths are prepared; no routing protocol or server backend is added.
implemented: Seventh ENARSI Layer3 lab with independent practice/completed variants, seven-row addressing/role plan, staged guide, tested reference commands, accessible counts and current-site domain/path/query permalinks. Existing ENARSI and39 ENCOR entries plus other categories remain available.

The normal baseline requires three actual client/server replies on each client through R2 with no classifier or policy configured. Correct extended ACLs, ordered route-map deny10/permit20 and two ingress bindings then steer only PC1 server requests through R3 while R1 RIB and ordinary CEF lookup continue to point to R2.

Selected traffic proof correlates three policy events with the same request IDs, correct ingress, R1 egress, downstream router sends, destination acceptance and parent-linked delivered replies. Real selected counters must advance, but counters or only two requests cannot fabricate the outcome.

PC1 diagnostic requests match route-map deny10 and are delivered using R2 normal forwarding. PC2 server requests match the classification ACL deny, do not match the permit clause and also remain delivered through R2. These checks distinguish classification and policy exemptions from interface packet filtering.

Ingress-binding removal and a nonmatching classifier source each require three real normal-path replies before restoration and fresh policy-path replies. Configuration-only toggles cannot count as repairs.

Shutting R1 Gi0/2 makes the directly adjacent policy next hop unavailable; successful traffic uses the R2 RIB route until restoration and fresh R3 delivery. A native counterfactual leaves that link up but disables R3 forwarding: policy is still selected and the failed delivery cannot be credited as end-to-end tracked fallback.

The default-next-hop exercise requires three observed stages: normal R2 forwarding under an explicit service /24, policy R3 forwarding when only a normal0/0 remains, and new R3 forwarding after restoring the explicit /24 and ordinary set ip next-hop action. Skipping the explicit-prefix comparison cannot earn it.

The local-policy exercise first proves router-originated ping uses R2 despite interface policy, then proves a temporary LOCAL-PBR map redirects actual router requests through R3. Removing the temporary global binding and map plus fresh intended client steering complete restoration. Skipping the normal local-origin stage cannot earn it.

Both clients must receive complete actual HTTP200 responses on their respective selected/normal request paths. Fourteen tasks combine four live configuration/state/save goals and ten observations. Practice starts0/14; completed reference supplies4/14 with no fabricated traffic or counters. Earned observations survive export/import, while health and startup equality revoke on drift.

Per-attempt epochs and normal simulator notifications capture synchronous CLI evidence with a closed guide. Exact route sets, canonical links, gateways, input bindings and policy clauses reject shortcuts and drift. No simulation engine, protocol implementation, global UI, terminal styling or artwork changed.
scope: Classic IOS IPv4 PBR with directly connected next hops. Native/browser validation does not claim a fresh CML capture. This lab does not configure recursive policy next hops, IP SLA verify-availability, VRFs, IPv6 PBR or NX-OS. Adjacent-link fallback is explicitly distinguished from remote health tracking.
